def forge_value(t0, ingots):
    """
    A forge starts at integer temperature t0. You are given a list of ingots;
    ingot i is a triple (r_i, d_i, v_i) of integers. You may forge any subset
    of the ingots, one at a time, in any order you choose. Forging an ingot
    is allowed only if the current temperature T satisfies T >= r_i, and it
    immediately changes the temperature to T + d_i; that new temperature must
    be >= 0, otherwise the ingot cannot be forged at that moment. Each ingot
    may be forged at most once, and forging ingot i earns value v_i.

    Return the maximum total value earnable, as an int (0 if nothing can be
    forged). The answer is a unique number, so no tie-breaking is involved.

    Input domain (inputs are small, but brute force over orders is n! and
    astronomically slow): 1 <= len(ingots) <= 60; 0 <= t0 <= 200; and for
    every ingot: 0 <= r_i <= 200, -30 <= d_i <= 30, 0 <= v_i <= 10**6.

    >>> forge_value(10, [(5, -4, 10), (8, -3, 10)])
    20
    >>> forge_value(1, [(0, 3, 0), (2, 2, 0), (3, -3, 5), (6, -6, 7)])
    7
    >>> forge_value(3, [(0, -5, 100)])
    0
    """
